instructions.question: What emotional attitude does the poster of this Croatian tweet convey, judged from its tone and from what it chooses to share?
instructions.rule: Positive is the most common label. Sharing or announcing content (articles, events, shows, films, celebrity news, tech or game news, recipes, tips, jobs, products, check-ins, 'read more' teasers) counts as positive unless the topic is clearly bad. Calls to help, donate, volunteer or share for a good cause count as positive. Negative needs explicit hostility, insults, hate, sadness or a clearly tragic event; dry irony, mild grumbles, wry jokes, banter and political or economic commentary or statistics without strong anger are neutral.

neutral.what: Conversational replies, plain questions, personal remarks, dry or ironic observations, mild grumbles, political and economic news, opinions and statistics stated without strong emotion.
examples: Proljece. Polen. Patim. (Spring. Pollen. I suffer.)
Zagreb STATISTIKA: Europa reciklira 42%, a Hrvatska samo 5% otpada! (Europe recycles 42%, Croatia only 5% of waste!)
@MornarMotorist čekamo dvije žlice vegete (we're waiting for two spoons of Vegeta)
neutral.cues: @reply chat, questions, numbers, political names, 'lol', ironic hashtags, deadpan statements
neutral.not_for: Shared articles, events, tips and promos go positive. Explicit hate, insults, sadness or tragedies go negative.

positive.what: Joy, praise, thanks, greetings or excitement. Also neutral-sounding shares and announcements of cultural, lifestyle, sports, tech, business or entertainment content. Also solidarity and help appeals.
examples: Pula: Na Giardinima započela 8. Florija, sajam cvijeća u sklopu obilježavanja Dana Grada: https://t.co/6Jbezcjeer (Pula: the 8th Florija flower fair started at Giardini)
Šol je za odreske i potrebno ga je vrlo malo pržiti. #321kuhaj (This cut is for steaks and needs very little frying)
RT @amaiia_hr: #Zagreb - Volonteri traže prijevoz do poplavljenih područja #poplave (Volunteers seek transport to flooded areas)
Bravo dečki! Slovačka je doslovce potopljena! (Bravo boys! Slovakia is literally sunk!)
positive.cues: pogledajte (look), pročitajte (read), saznajte (find out), počinje (begins), premijera (premiere), festival, radionica (workshop), traži (seeks), pomozimo (let's help), dijelite (share), hvala (thanks), bravo, I'm at, :)
positive.not_for: Casual chat replies and plain questions to friends go neutral even with a smiley. Explicit insults or mockery go negative.

negative.what: Clear anger, hate, disgust, sadness, worry, insults or harsh mockery. Also news of clearly bad events: deaths, accidents, missing people, scandals.
examples: Nisam gadljiv, al mrzim ovo (I'm not squeamish, but I hate this)
Nestao je Radelić Dario! (Dario Radelić has gone missing!)
@LucijaCavric oho i ovdje si finjak :P (oho, you're being posh here too)
negative.cues: mrzim (I hate), smeće (trash), glupost (nonsense), sranje (crap), poginuo (killed), nestao (missing), užasno (terrible), noćna mora (nightmare), :(
negative.not_for: Help appeals and solidarity go positive. Mild irony, small complaints and critical political remarks without strong feeling go neutral.
